If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid overestimating upward momentum.

If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early-horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for downward bias.

If sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 3 days, shift forecast midpoint downward by 2–3% and apply a 1% decay per day for the following 5 days.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late-horizon (days 20–30) to capture momentum carryover.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for late-horizon to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is consistently bullish but forecast is below 65% of recent high, apply a 1–2% upward adjustment for mid-horizon to align with sentiment-driven breakout expectations.
